mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 3% for three consecutive months signals a stagflationary environment, where higher rates and inflation erode real corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both > 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 3% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related sectors and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when HOUST is above its 12-month MA for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both PAYEMS (payroll employment) and UNRATE (unemployment rate) where PAYEMS increases while UNRATE falls below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market with low slack, which supports wage growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE < 5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE < 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates households are drawing down savings to sustain consumption, which temporarily supports demand but ultimately signals weaker future growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
